problem: Existing photo-realistic VLN datasets are English-only and small. R2R has about 22K instructions and 7K paths. R2R paths are short shortest-paths of 4–6 edges, which carry strong length and goal-seeking priors that agents exploit without using language. These datasets also lack fine-grained word-to-visual grounding and human follower demonstrations.
motivation: Findings from high-resource languages may not generalize, and different languages encode spatial and temporal relations differently. VLN also suffers from scarce training data. Because prior agents exploited path biases, success could come from ignoring the instruction. The authors observe that annotators attend to a narrow part of the panorama (27–28% after the first viewpoint) and to the instruction words said or heard so far. Time-aligned human pose traces could therefore supervise agents far more densely than path-level labels.
key_idea: Collect a large multilingual VLN dataset (RxR) with these properties: guides speak instructions natively in English, Hindi and Telugu; paths are sampled to be long and varied, non-shortest and well-covered; every word is time-aligned to the guide's and a validating follower's 6-DOF virtual pose trace.
insight: Path design matters. A 'correct first step then go straight' heuristic gets 27.2 SR on R2R but only 13.7 on RxR val-unseen, so RxR largely removes the go-straight / length prior. Human follower paths are useful extra supervision: training on Guide+Follower paths beats Guide-only or Follower-only for every language (exp 3 vs 1, 2). More languages in one model hurts; the monolingual agents average 28.5 SR vs 22.8 for the multilingual agent on val-unseen, and adding MT cross-translations degrades further (exp 5). Unimodal ablations show both modalities are needed: language-only reaches 16.0–18.0 SR and vision-only 7.8. Supervising attention with pose traces gave only mixed gains: better NDTW/NE, worse SR.
method: Two-level path sampling: build a room graph from Matterport3D room annotations. Enumerate simple room paths of at most 5 rooms and 2 levels. Sample start and goal panoramas in the first and last rooms, then take the shortest panorama path inside the subgraph induced by that room sequence. The resulting paths are non-shortest overall, high-variance in length and natural to describe.

Greedy coverage selection: repeatedly pick the path minimizing d(p1,pm)/L(path) + the mean prior occurrence count of its panoramas. Constraints are ≤40 m and ≤500 paths per building. The result is 16,522 paths (11,089 train / 1,232 val-seen / 1,517 val-unseen / 2,684 test), 8 edges and 14.9 m on average, 44.5% not shortest.

Guide annotation with pose traces: in a web Matterport3D simulator (640×480, 75° vFOV) guides speak while moving along the path and later transcribe their own audio. The transcript is aligned to timestamped ASR output with DTW, giving word-level alignment to 6-DOF camera poses. Each language gets 14K paths × 3 instructions (126K total, avg 78 words).

Follower validation/demonstrations: other annotators listen to the audio and try to follow it. If the follower does not reach within 3 m of the goal, the instruction goes to a second follower or the path is re-annotated. Follower pose traces are released as alternative human demonstration paths (F-paths). Human SR is 93.9 on test.

Baseline agent: RCM-style seq2seq. A residual 1D-CNN instruction encoder runs over multilingual BERT features. An LSTM decoder uses dot-product attention over 36 panoramic view features (EfficientNet-B4, dual-encoder pretrained on Conceptual Captions, plus angle encodings) and over the instruction. Actions are scored as h_t · navigable-direction features.

Training: implemented in VALAN. Each batch is 50% behavior cloning on gold paths and 50% policy-gradient rollouts, with reward = incremental NDTW plus a linear navigation-error term at stop. Adam, 100K iterations, batch 32, lr 1e-4.

Spatiotemporal grounding supervision: pose traces are converted to text masks b_t (words spoken or heard up to step t) and visual masks max-pooled to 36 views (m_t). When on the gold path, a cross-entropy loss log Σ exp(z) − log Σ m·exp(z) pushes attention away from features the annotators never observed.

setting.backbone: RCM-style LSTM seq2seq agent with residual 1D-CNN instruction encoder over (frozen) multilingual BERT features and EfficientNet-B4 image features pretrained as image-text dual encoder on Conceptual Captions; policy trained on RxR
setting.training_data: RxR train: Guide + Follower paths, 84K instruction-path pairs per language for monolingual agents, 252K for the multilingual agent. Optional variants add Google-MT cross-translations (504K pairs) or R2R train (multitask). CNN pretrained on Conceptual Captions.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views, pre-extracted CNN features + heading/elevation encodings)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (select navigable direction or stop)
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (VALAN framework; custom web-based Matterport3D annotation tool)

numbers_note: This is a dataset paper; the agents are baselines. 'en' merges en-US and en-IN. Language-averaged (avg) scores are printed only for Mono/Multi in the test-results table, so for other variants only per-language values are given. RxR SPL is printed only per-language, in the multitask table. Test numbers are on Test-Standard. Not included: simple heuristic baselines (random walk, go-straight), unimodal ablations (language-only exp. 9: SR 16.0/18.0/16.9; vision-only exp. 10: SR 7.8), cross-translation exp. 5, human follower results (test SR 93.9 avg).
results: RxR has 126K instructions (78 words on average vs 29 in R2R) over 16.5K paths in three languages, with dense pose-trace grounding and 126K follower demonstrations. Humans reach 93.9 SR / 79.5 nDTW on test-standard. The best baseline agents, monolingual RCM-style ones, reach only 25.9 SR / 41.5 nDTW (multilingual: 21.3 / 37.2; random: 7.5 / 15.4), leaving large headroom. Heuristics that exploit path bias transfer poorly to RxR. Multitask R2R+RxR training improves R2R val-unseen over R2R-only training (SR 36.5→37.8, SPL 31.7→34.3, nDTW 48.1→52.3) with no loss on RxR.
limitations: Baseline agent is a comparatively weak LSTM/RCM-style model. Pose-trace grounding supervision is only a preliminary exploration with mixed results, and textual-attention supervision did not help.
Guide audio was not released at publication (privacy review due to COVID-19 home annotation). Cross-language differences cannot be disentangled from annotator-pool conventions.
Discrete nav-graph setting only; perspective-camera or continuous (VLN-CE) versions are left to future work. A multilingual single agent underperforms monolingual agents.
